identity.name: BUGSTER AI-Assisted WordPress Brute Force to MongoDB Exfil and PowerShell C2 — EDR + NGFW + AI Access Stitch (T1110.001 / T1041)
identity.summary: A financially motivated actor (BUGSTER) drives Hermes Agent on DeepSeek V4 under a system-prompt override to generate its tooling: WordPress author enumeration through the REST API and author sitemaps, a 117x28 wp-login brute force, a MongoDB dump with a manifest, and exfil plus a VBScript-delivered Base64 PowerShell reverse shell to one actor server.
identity.description: Unit 42 (2026-10-21) documents BUGSTER, who configured the Hermes Agent framework with DeepSeek V4 (safety controls overridden by a system prompt) and Cursor IDE to plan and execute cybercrime. Against one Indian university the actor enumerated 12 subdomains and 13 WordPress authors via post author fields and author sitemaps (bypassing a WAF block on the user endpoint), then ran a generated brute-force tool of 117 usernames x 28 passwords that recorded one valid login. Against a second university it exfiltrated a MongoDB database with an admin account with a weak password, writing a manifest of records and exposed infrastructure. One US server, 162.243.3.92, hosted Hermes Agent, a Python C2 listener for Windows reverse shells (a Base64 PowerShell shell delivered via VBScript) and a Cursor IDE proxy; 104.238.38.202 is a commercial proxy server. A dedicated script sent the safety override to GLM 5.2; other models were tested through OpenRouter. SIM-MP-035 reproduces the recon, brute force, dump, staging and reverse-shell lineage on a Linux foothold against a lab stage host, emits NGFW EAL records from the same host to both published IPs, and sends real GenAI egress with fake keys carrying the jailbreak override to DeepSeek and OpenRouter; CR-MP-0035 fuses EDR, NDR and AI Access alerts on src_host.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-035 — BUGSTER AI-assisted WordPress brute force to MongoDB exfil and PowerShell C2, EDR + NGFW + AI Access stitch

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR agent on the Linux host playing the actor's foothold, and an XSIAM HTTP log collector (or Broker VM) the NGFW EAL records can be POSTed to.
A lab stage host answering the WordPress REST / sitemap / wp-login shapes, TCP 27017 and the :4444 listener (STAGE_HOST); no traffic goes to actor infrastructure.
Outbound HTTPS from the foothold to api.deepseek.com and openrouter.ai through the inspected egress path (AI Access Security); the requests carry fake keys and are rejected by the providers.

payload.code:
# Safe chain: every HTTP / MongoDB / :4444 request goes to the lab stage host; the published IPs
# appear only as NGFW EAL record fields; the dump holds synthetic records only.
# See scenarios/multi_plane/mp-035-bugster-ai-assisted-wordpress-to-mongodb-exfil.yml steps 01-09.
mkdir -p /tmp/cortexsim-mp-035
python3 -c 'import os,urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request("http://"+os.environ.get("STAGE_HOST","127.0.0.1")+"/wp-sitemap-users-1.xml",headers={"User-Agent":"python-requests/2.31.0"}),timeout=5)' || true

input_variables.name: COLLECTOR_URL
input_variables.description: XSIAM HTTP log collector the NGFW EAL records are POSTed to.

iocs.context: Actor infrastructure (IOC section: 162.243.3[.]92): one US server hosting Hermes Agent, the Python C2 listener and the Cursor IDE proxy. Destination of the NGFW EAL upload and reverse-shell records.
Commercial proxy server (IOC section: 104.238.38[.]202). Destination of the NGFW EAL proxy records the brute force tunnels through.

biocs.name: MP-035 python3 Enumerates WordPress Authors via the REST API and Author Sitemap
biocs.description: python3 requests WordPress post author fields (/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?_fields=author,author_name) and the author sitemap (/wp-sitemap-users-1.xml) with a python-requests user agent: author enumeration that sidesteps a WAF block on /wp/v2/users.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter action_remote_port in (80, 443)
| filter http_url contains "wp-sitemap-users" or http_url contains "_fields=author" or http_url contains "/wp-json/wp/v2/users"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, http_url, user_agent, causality_actor_process_image_name

biocs.name: MP-035 python3 Writes a Candidate Credential File After Repeated wp-login POSTs
biocs.description: A python3 process that has just sent many POSTs to /wp-login.php writes a text file of candidate credentials (valid_candidates.txt): the generated brute-force tool recording a hit.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter action_file_name ~= "(valid|candidate|cred|found).*\.txt$"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_command_line, action_file_path

biocs.name: MP-035 python3 Dumps a MongoDB and Writes an Exfiltration Manifest
biocs.description: Under a python3 causality chain, mongodump or python3 connects to TCP 27017 and the chain writes collection files plus manifest.json into one dump directory: database exfiltration tooling with a manifest of what it took.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter (event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and action_remote_port = 27017) or (event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_name = "manifest.json") or (event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and action_process_image_name = "mongodump")
| comp count() as events, values(action_file_name) as files, values(action_remote_ip) as dbs by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter array_length(files) > 0

biocs.name: MP-035 tar Compresses a Database Dump Under a python3 Causality Chain
biocs.description: tar -czf with a python3 parent archives a directory holding manifest.json and collection dumps into a .tar.gz: staging the dump for exfiltration.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "tar" and actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "-czf" and (action_process_image_command_line contains "dump" or action_process_image_command_line contains "records")
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: MP-035 Shell Under python3 Opens a Reverse Shell Over dev tcp to Port 4444
biocs.description: bash with a python3 parent runs a command line that opens /dev/tcp/<host>/4444: a reverse shell to a C2 listener port.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh") and actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python", "timeout")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "/dev/tcp/" and action_process_image_command_line contains "/4444"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, action_process_image_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name

biocs.name: MP-035 wscript Launches Hidden PowerShell With an EncodedCommand TCPClient
biocs.description: wscript.exe running a .vbs starts powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -EncodedCommand whose decoded text creates Net.Sockets.TCPClient: a Base64 PowerShell reverse shell delivered via VBScript.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_process_image_name = "wscript.exe" and action_process_image_name = "powershell.exe"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "-EncodedCommand" and action_process_image_command_line contains "hidden"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_command_line, action_process_image_command_line

biocs.name: MP-035 Jailbreak System-Prompt Override Sent to an Unsanctioned GenAI Provider
biocs.description: AI Access Security: requests from a host to unsanctioned GenAI APIs (api.deepseek.com and openrouter.ai) whose prompts carry a jailbreak / safety-override frame; both providers receive the override. The validation logic confirms the sessions to both on the NGFW; the content verdict is AI Access Security's.
biocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter url_domain in ("api.deepseek.com", "openrouter.ai") or dst_hostname in ("api.deepseek.com", "openrouter.ai")
| comp count() as sessions, values(dst_hostname) as providers by endpoint_device_name, src
| filter array_length(providers) >= 2

abiocs.name: MP-035 Scripted wp-login Credential Burst From a Host Process
abiocs.description: A non-browser process (python3) sends a high-rate burst of HTTP POSTs to one /wp-login.php URI (dozens within seconds, several accounts): scripted password guessing from the host. Linux network events do not reliably carry http_url / http_method, so the fallback counts web-port connections per process instance and destination.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter (http_url contains "wp-login.php" and http_method = "POST") or action_remote_port in (80, 443)
| bin _time span = 1m
| comp count() as posts by agent_hostname, actor_process_instance_id, action_remote_ip, _time
| filter posts >= 20
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned host baseline -> first-seen POST rate to a login URI from a scripting interpreter, anchored to actor_process_instance_id under the python3 causality chain.

abiocs.name: MP-035 NGFW Recurring python3 Sessions to an External HTTP Proxy
abiocs.description: NGFW EAL recurring sessions whose endpoint process is python3 to an external HTTP proxy rare across the fleet: tooling tunnelled through a commercial proxy.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter process_name in ("python3", "python") and app = "http-proxy"
| comp count() as sessions by endpoint_device_name, dst, dst_port
| filter sessions >= 5
abiocs.causality_anchor: Fleet baseline -> rare external proxy destination from a scripting interpreter, anchored on endpoint_device_name.

abiocs.name: MP-035 NGFW Large Upload From python3 to a Rare External IP on Port 8080
abiocs.description: One NGFW EAL session whose endpoint process is python3 sends an anomalously large bytes_sent to a rare external IP on a non-standard web port.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter process_name in ("python3", "python") and dst_port = 8080
| filter bytes_sent > 50000000
| fields _time, endpoint_device_name, src, dst, dst_port, app, bytes_sent, process_name
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-host upload baseline -> first large outbound transfer to a rare destination, anchored on endpoint_device_name and process_name.

abiocs.name: MP-035 NGFW Recurring Communications to the Actor Server on Port 4444
abiocs.description: NGFW EAL recurring small sessions whose endpoint process is a shell (bash on Linux; powershell.exe on the Windows variant) to an external IP on port 4444: reverse-shell callback cadence.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter process_name in ("bash", "sh", "powershell.exe") and dst_port = 4444
| comp count() as sessions by endpoint_device_name, dst
| filter sessions >= 4
abiocs.causality_anchor: Fleet baseline -> recurring cadence to a rare destination on a non-standard port, anchored on endpoint_device_name.

xql_queries.name: MP-035 python3 Recon Lineage Writes an Enumeration Report and Probes WordPress User Endpoints
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("python3", "python")
| filter (event_type = ENUM.FILE and action_file_name = "enumeration_report.json") or (event_type = ENUM.NETWORK and (http_url contains "wp-json" or http_url contains "wp-sitemap-users"))
| comp count() as events, values(action_file_name) as files by agent_hostname

xql_queries.name: MP-035 NGFW Traffic From the Run Host to Published BUGSTER Infrastructure
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter dst in ("162.243.3.92", "104.238.38.202")
| comp count() as sessions, values(dst) as dsts, values(dst_port) as ports by endpoint_device_name
| filter array_length(dsts) >= 2

xql_queries.name: MP-035 GenAI Egress From the Run Host to DeepSeek and OpenRouter
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter url_domain in ("api.deepseek.com", "openrouter.ai") or dst_hostname in ("api.deepseek.com", "openrouter.ai")
| comp count() as sessions, values(dst_hostname) as providers by endpoint_device_name, src

xql_queries.name: MP-035 One Incident Holds the Endpoint, NGFW and AI Access Alerts
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xsiam_incidents
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter description contains "CR-MP-0035" or name contains "BUGSTER"
| fields _time, incident_id, name, hosts, alert_sources

correlation_rules.name: BUGSTER AI-Assisted Intrusion — python3 Tooling, Proxy / Exfil / C2 Traffic and a GenAI Jailbreak on One Host
correlation_rules.logic: (BIOC(MP-035 python3 Enumerates WordPress Authors via the REST API and Author Sitemap) OR ABIOC(MP-035 Scripted wp-login Credential Burst From a Host Process) OR BIOC(MP-035 python3 Dumps a MongoDB and Writes an Exfiltration Manifest) OR BIOC(MP-035 tar Compresses a Database Dump Under a python3 Causality Chain) OR BIOC(MP-035 Shell Under python3 Opens a Reverse Shell Over dev tcp to Port 4444) OR BIOC(MP-035 wscript Launches Hidden PowerShell With an EncodedCommand TCPClient)) AND (ABIOC(MP-035 NGFW Recurring python3 Sessions to an External HTTP Proxy) OR ABIOC(MP-035 NGFW Large Upload From python3 to a Rare External IP on Port 8080) OR ABIOC(MP-035 NGFW Recurring Communications to the Actor Server on Port 4444) OR IOC(162.243.3.92) OR IOC(104.238.38.202)) AND BIOC(MP-035 Jailbreak System-Prompt Override Sent to an Unsanctioned GenAI Provider) within 3600s on the same endpoint entity (xdr_data agent_hostname = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw endpoint_device_name = the AI Access source host, the src_host every leg carries) -> one BUGSTER incident whose summary names the python3 tooling lineage, the proxy and actor-server destinations and the jailbreak attempts to both providers.

correlation_rules.name: MP-035 network-leg fusion — NGFW proxy, bulk-upload and beacon sessions on one host
correlation_rules.logic: panw_ngfw_traffic_raw (python3 recurring sessions to the external HTTP proxy, step-03) JOIN panw_ngfw_traffic_raw (large python3 upload to the rare external IP on port 8080, step-06) JOIN panw_ngfw_traffic_raw (recurring bash sessions to the actor server 162.243.3.92 on port 4444, step-08) ON endpoint_device_name (with src as the tie-break when the hostname is absent) WHERE all three fall within 3600s of each other -> one network-plane finding for the run host; feeds CR-MP-0035 as its network leg. Joins only NGFW records; no endpoint, AI Access or cloud dataset.

threat_scenarios.name: BUGSTER AI-Assisted Intrusion — Tooling Lineage, Network Egress and GenAI Misuse in One Incident
threat_scenarios.description: The python3 tooling lineage, its proxy / exfil / C2 traffic and the GenAI jailbreak egress raise alerts on three sensors that XSIAM fuses on the foothold.

threat_steps.objective: Endpoint alerts fire on the python3 tooling: WordPress recon, wp-login burst, MongoDB dump with manifest, tar staging and the 4444 reverse shell.
preconditions: XDR agent on the Linux foothold host.
steps: Run steps 01, 02, 04, 05 and 07 as the www-data foothold user.
Open the causality view of python3.
success_criteria: The BIOCs and ABIOC for steps 01-07 fire under the python3 causality chain.

threat_steps.objective: NGFW EAL records to both published IPs land on the same host and IOC enrichment names BUGSTER.
preconditions: NGFW EAL records POSTed to the tenant collector.
steps: Search panw_ngfw_traffic_raw for endpoint_device_name = the run host.
success_criteria: panw_ngfw_traffic_raw shows the run host to 104.238.38.202 and 162.243.3.92.

threat_steps.objective: AI Access Security flags the jailbreak override sent to both DeepSeek and OpenRouter, and CR-MP-0035 fuses all three legs.
preconditions: Egress to api.deepseek.com and openrouter.ai is inspected by AI Access Security.
steps: Open the incident for the run host.
success_criteria: AI Access Security raises the jailbreak verdict for both api.deepseek.com and openrouter.ai.
Exactly one incident holds the endpoint, NGFW and AI Access alerts.

preventive_controls: Rate-limit and MFA-protect wp-login.php, and restrict REST API author fields and author sitemaps on public WordPress sites.
Never expose MongoDB to the internet; enforce strong admin credentials and network allow-lists.
Block unsanctioned GenAI providers (DeepSeek, OpenRouter) with AI Access Security and the published IPs with Advanced IP Defense / EDL.
detection_engineering: Alert on scripting interpreters posting repeatedly to login URIs from servers and workstations.
Alert on wscript.exe starting hidden PowerShell with -EncodedCommand.
Correlate endpoint tooling alerts with GenAI jailbreak verdicts and rare-destination egress on the same host.
